finding.claim: Xxh32::update truncates input.len() to u32 in the fast-path check, then copies the full untruncated slice into the 16-byte mem buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write in release builds when a single update input length is a multiple of 2^32 (or otherwise has low 32 bits below 16 - mem_size).
finding.source: Public Xxh32::update(&mut self, input: &[u8]) at src/xxh32.rs:102; attacker-controlled slice of length >= 4 GiB (e.g. exactly 2^32 bytes) in one call.
finding.sink: src/xxh32.rs:111 Buffer{ptr: self.mem.as_mut_ptr(), len: 16, offset: mem_size}.copy_from_slice(input) -> src/utils.rs:39-48 ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(src, ptr.add(offset), src.len()).

trace.note: total_len wraps via input.len() as u32 (harmless for memory)
fast-path test uses input.len() as u32 truncation: for len=2^32, 0 + 0 < 16 is true
copy_from_slice(input) copies full src.len() (usize) bytes into 16-byte mem buffer
only bounds check is debug_assert, compiled out in release
ptr::copy_nonoverlapping with len = src.len() (>= 4 GiB) writes past mem
mem_size += input.len() as u32 also truncated

finding.guards_checked: Line 106 truncated u32 comparison (the only length guard on this path, wrong width); utils.rs:45 debug_assert (release-only); xxh32.rs:116 mem_size>0 branch (not reached for this input); xxh64.rs equivalent uses usize and is not affected; xxh3.rs streaming buffer and get_unchecked(len-1) sites in 1to3 helpers verified safe by dispatch guards (len 1-3 only) and in-range offsets.
